workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§115–120
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§115–120: Sworn Brotherhood Renewed and the Gathering of the Host
part: §§115–120 — Sworn Brotherhood Renewed and the Gathering of the Host
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§115–120, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Six sections. §115 follows Temüjin, Jamuqa and Qan To'oril as they pull down the Merkid camps and withdraw. §116 tells how the boys Temüjin and Jamuqa first became sworn brothers on the ice of the Onan, with the exchange of knucklebones and arrowheads. §117 has them renew the vow and exchange the belts and horses taken from the Merkid. §118 is the parting at the camp-move, Jamuqa's riddle and Börte-Üjin's reading of it. §119 carries them through the night past the Taichi'ud and gives a boy to Högelün. §120 is a long list of who came to join Temüjin at dawn.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.l: Temüžin, To'oril Qān, Žamuqa, three together joining,
sentences.i: Temüjin, Qan To'oril and Jamuqa joined together, the three of them,
sentences.n: A short opening clause with no verb of its own: qamtudču (Ming 相同着, 'together', a converb) hangs on the verb ičuba at the end of unit 3. The subjects are the three men, Temüžin, Toγ̇oril Qān and Žamuqa, and γurban 'three' stands before qamtudču to count them. The title Qān (Ming 皇帝) is the short form beside qaγan and follows the name.

sentences.i: Kinggijadai of the Olqunu'ud, Sechigür from the Qorolas and Möchibedügün from the Dörben came.

sentences.l: Ikires's Butu here as-son-in-law going-about-because came.
sentences.i: Butu of the Ikires came, because he had been living here as a son-in-law.
sentences.n: kürege-te (做女婿) is 'as a son-in-law'; the ending -te I leave open. jabuγsaγ̇ar (行來的上頭) is 'because of having gone about'; the Ming 的上頭 means 'on account of' and the ending is uncertain; 'going about as a son-in-law' I render as 'living here as a son-in-law'. ende (這裏) 'here'.
